sec: Prolactinoma prevalence, clinical syndrome and MRI features

items.q: What is the female-to-male ratio in patients diagnosed with microprolactinoma?
items.exp: Microprolactinomas show a marked female preponderance with an F:M ratio of 20:1. (Book p943)

items.q: Assess gender patterns in prolactinomas: I Macroprolactinomas have an equal female-to-male ratio of 1:1. II Men with prolactinoma typically present late with compressive mass effects.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Macroprolactinomas show F:M = 1:1 because men lack menstrual cues and present late with mass effects. (Book p943)

items.q: Match the patient age group to its prolactinoma clinical pattern — 1) 25 to 45 years 2) Less than 20 years … A) Most common peak age of presentation B) Genetic/syndromic causes (MEN 1, McCune-Albright, Carney complex)
items.exp: Peak incidence occurs at 25-45 years; presentations under 20 suggest MEON syndromes (MEN 1, McCune-Albright, Carney). (Book p943)

items.q: In the galactorrhea-amenorrhea complex, hyperprolactinemia suppresses the hypothalamo-pituitary-gonadal axis leading to hypogonadism and ___.
items.exp: Elevated prolactin inhibits the HPG axis, producing hypogonadism and luteolysis. (Book p943)

items.q: A 29-year-old female presents with secondary amenorrhea, milky breast discharge, and hot flushes. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) demonstrates osteopenia localized predominantly to the:
items.exp: Hypogonadism in hyperprolactinemia leads to osteopenia and osteoporosis involving predominantly the spine. (Book p943)

items.q: Why does hypogonadism in males with prolactinoma often go unnoticed until late stages?
opts: Symptoms such as loss of libido and erectile dysfunction are subtle and insidious
Testosterone levels are paradoxically maintained by direct adrenal stimulation
Gynaecomastia occurs in 100% of cases providing an immediate visible cue
Men do not experience bone density loss from hypogonadism
items.exp: In males, hypogonadal symptoms like loss of libido and erectile dysfunction go unnoticed until mass effects emerge. (Book p943)

items.q: What percentage of patients harboring a macroprolactinoma present with visual field defects?
items.exp: In macroprolactinomas, 35% of patients have visual field defects and 45% have hypopituitarism of other axes. (Book p943)

items.q: In patients with macroprolactinoma, what proportion demonstrate deficiency of other anterior pituitary hormones?
items.exp: Deficiency of other pituitary hormones is found in 45% of macroprolactinoma patients. (Book p943)

items.q: What is the confirmatory investigation of choice (IOC) for suspected prolactinoma?
opts: Basal serum prolactin measurement at 8 AM
TRH dynamic stimulation testing with serum prolactin curve
items.exp: The confirmatory investigation of choice is Gadolinium-enhanced MRI (T1 sagittal post-contrast). (Book p943)

items.q: Assess the MRI appearance of a pituitary microadenoma: I Pre-contrast features include gland asymmetry, depression of the sellar floor, and infundibular stalk deviation. II Post-contrast imaging shows the whole normal gland enhancing except the hypointense adenoma.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Pre-contrast microadenoma signs are asymmetry, floor depression, and stalk deviation; with contrast, the normal gland enhances while the adenoma remains hypoenhancing. (Book p943)

items.q: A 35-year-old male undergoes sellar MRI for bitemporal visual deficits. The coronal post-contrast sequence demonstrates a 2.5 cm heterogeneous mass composed of cystic (non-enhancing) and solid (enhancing) areas. This lesion is a:
items.exp: Macroprolactinomas characteristically show heterogeneous post-contrast enhancement with non-enhancing cystic areas and enhancing solid components. (Book p943)

items.q: Match the pituitary imaging finding on MRI to its structural entity — 1) Pre-contrast sellar floor depression and stalk deviation 2) Non-enhancing fluid compartment within macroadenoma 3) Diffuse uniform avid post-contrast enhancement … A) Microadenoma B) Cystic component C) Normal pituitary parenchyma
items.exp: Microadenomas produce floor depression and stalk deviation; cystic components do not enhance; normal pituitary parenchyma enhances uniformly. (Book p943)

items.q: Which syndrome is NOT part of the MEON genetic complex associated with young-onset prolactinomas (< 20 years)?
items.exp: Genetic syndromes associated with early prolactinomas include MEN 1, McCune-Albright, and Carney complex; MEN 2 is not linked to pituitary adenomas. (Book p943)
